summary: 1. One new meeting note this pass — a crusher-feed review naming grizzly-choking root causes in full for the first time (boulder interlocking that reads full from above while empty underneath, a design barrier limiting how far loaders can reach into the grid) and formalizing a 10% bin-trigger CCR-to-dispatch radio protocol, replacing reliance on WhatsApp for urgent low-bin escalation. 2. Sep 4 production reverses hard: ore misses target by -32.85% after two consecutive beats of +98.32% and +130.85%, the third large swing in three days. 3. Drilling keeps a fourth straight beat alive (+35.5%), but only because the daily target itself roughly halved (2,563 m to 1,281.5 m) — not a like-for-like acceleration. 4. No blast was recorded, the cycle's first blast-free day. 3. 5. Fleet: EX-247 recovers after a seven-day bucket/hose repair. 6. DT-108 relapses into its third distinct fault this week. 7. DT-79 surfaces in this KB for the first time as down since 1-Feb-26 — over seven months, worth confirming whether the record is live or stale. 8. Overall daily availability improves to 87.46% (MTD 86.42%). 4. 9. Survey Day 11 posts the cycle's deepest single-day gap yet (-53.34%, trucks 12,493 / survey 8,147) — and Abel Pienaar's response to it proposes a different kind of fix than anything logged before: dropping the truck conversion factor to 28, rather than addressing the boundary-compliance root cause. Flagged directly in [[survey-volume-reconciliation]] as a step that would shrink the reported gap without fixing why trucks and survey disagree, and would make future gaps incomparable to the Day 1-11 series already on record. 5. GM Ivan Anthony's 4-Sep email is the most detailed August root-cause analysis this KB has captured: the core issue was insufficient productive mining-face flexibility to absorb the visa-delay/breakdown disruptions, not the disruptions themselves. New precise monthly reconciliation figures (August survey 80.9% of target vs. truck tally 92.2%) sit alongside two new external-engagement commitments (an independent survey audit, and Outliers Mining Solutions for a recovery plan and optimized mining sequence) and a hard Sunday (7-Sep) deadline for a detailed action plan to Maaden. 6. A file missed by the 106th/107th passes' gap-checks was caught this pass: the wider-distribution circulation email for the already-compiled SA-185/DT-185 tire-fire flash report (5-Aug incident). No new incident content — registered for completeness. Seventeen already ingested at prior passes. One genuinely new: the crusher-feed review meeting, written verbatim to RAW. Important References folder re-checked: 39 files, no new content since the 105th pass's last check.
